slides.texte_overlay:
habits that make you look
smarter than you are

pausing before you answer

take a breath before replying to a question. a short pause makes your answer sound thoughtful, and it gives you time to say something much better and clearer.

using simple words

explain things in plain, simple words instead of big ones. people who can make hard ideas sound easy always come across as the smartest people in the room.

asking great questions

ask one thoughtful question instead of pretending to know. curious questions make you look engaged and intelligent, and you learn so much more along the way.

knowing a bit of everything

a little knowledge about art, history and science makes you sound sharp anywhere, and it only takes a few minutes a day. small, steady learning adds up faster than you'd expect.
slides.texte_sophia:
knowing a bit of everything

know a bit of everything. the Sophia app turns it into one short lesson a day, art, history or science, and 5 minutes is enough to sound sharp in any conversation.

slides.texte_overlay:
admitting what you don't know

saying i'm not sure, let me check, sounds far smarter than a confident guess. people trust those who are honest about the real limits of their knowledge.
